purpose: Follow restricted outcomes into a conditional probability with a new denominator.
meaning: Conditioning asks about one event after attention is restricted to another event of positive probability. Their intersection supplies the numerator; the conditioning event supplies the denominator. A uniform-location strip makes the lengths and the renormalization visible.

definition.setting: Conditional probability on a continuous uniform location model over one 100 cm strip.
definition.formal_latex: P(A\mid B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{\min(a,b)}{b},\quad P(A)=\frac{a}{100},\quad P(B)=\frac{b}{100},\quad b>0.

signature.a: Length of the inked prefix in centimetres.
signature.P(A|B): Conditional ink probability given the window.

conditions: A location is chosen uniformly along a 100 cm strip. Probabilities of intervals equal their lengths divided by 100 cm.
The inked event A is the first a cm and inspection event B is the first b cm: 0≤a≤100 cm and 0<b≤100 cm.
The two intervals share their left endpoint, so their overlap length is min(a,b). This specimen does not realize every relationship between two events.
Conditioning divides the overlap probability by positive P(B); a zero-length conditioning window is excluded.
definition.domain_notes: Generally, P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B) for P(B)>0. The first frame shares a physical length scale; the second explicitly normalizes B to unit probability. This does not alter P(A).
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources; restricted-family properties are author-derived. Independent review pending.

prompts.prompt: Did the ink itself change when the window narrowed?
prompts.answer: No. The inked length and its original probability remain fixed; the denominator changes.

prompts.prompt: Can the inspection window have length zero?
prompts.answer: Not in the elementary ratio definition: that would make P(B)=0.
